summary: The run established a strong offensive and exhaust-oriented Ironclad shell, but it accumulated severe Act 2 attrition and ended with only 17 HP in the Gremlin Leader fight. The clearest strategic issue was repeatedly trading away the Sapphire Key for relics, while later card rewards continued adding redundant damage rather than improving the deck's ability to survive difficult multi-enemy fights.

lessons.title: Do not trade away a required key without an intentional Act 3 plan
lessons.situation: When offered a choice between a colored key and a linked relic, especially if the run is still pursuing the full-key route.
lessons.lesson: Take the Sapphire Key unless deliberately abandoning the Act 3 key objective. A useful relic is not worth permanently losing access to the corresponding key path when the run may otherwise survive to Act 3.
evidence_points: Act 1 Floor 9: the run chose Meat on the Bone and gave up the Sapphire Key.
Act 2 Floor 26: the run again chose Dream Catcher and gave up the Sapphire Key.
The final keys were ruby=True, emerald=False, sapphire=False.
lessons.reasoning: Both key opportunities were declined, so the run was guaranteed to finish without the Sapphire Key regardless of later combat performance. This is a reusable planning error rather than merely a symptom of the final loss.

lessons.title: Stop adding marginal attacks once the damage package is established
lessons.situation: When the deck already contains several efficient attacks and later rewards offer another copy or upgrade with limited defensive or scaling value.
lessons.lesson: Prefer skipping redundant damage rewards or taking cards that improve defense, scaling, or exhaust consistency. In particular, reassess duplicate Angers, Thunderclaps, and Perfected Strikes instead of continuing to enlarge an already attack-heavy deck.
evidence_points: The run took Carnage, Perfected Strike, Anger, another Anger+, Thunderclap, and Perfected Strike+ across the run.
The final 30-card deck still contained three Strikes, two Perfected Strikes including Perfected Strike+, Anger, Anger+, and Thunderclap.
Act 2 combat attrition was severe: HP fell from 89 after Floor 21 combat to 21 after Floor 23 combat, then to 15 after Floor 24 combat.
lessons.reasoning: The final build had a substantial damage package, yet the deck continued accepting marginal attack additions while losing most of its HP in consecutive Act 2 fights. Once damage is sufficient, reward decisions should address survivability and consistency rather than further increasing redundant attack density.
